newsitem.title: THAILAND: Dealers suspect BOT intervenes on heavy baht sales.
newsitem.headline: Dealers suspect BOT intervenes on heavy baht sales.

text.p: Some currency dealers said they believed the Bank of Thailand had intervened to defend the baht in the Singapore market during midday Wednesday but the central bank did not confirm it.

They said the market saw heavy selling offers on baht, mostly from Singapore dealers shortly before noon, on renewed jitters over Thai economic policies and speculation about a possible change in the Thai finance portfolio.
Central bank officials declined to comment whether the bank had intervened.
The baht fell to 26.250-26.300 to the dollar before it recovered to 26.030-26.080 at 0656 GMT. The central bank fixed the baht/dollar midrate at 25.86 on Wednesday against 25.88 on Tuesday.
"I heard that the central bank intervened, otherwise the baht could not stage such a comeback," a Thai bank dealer.
Dealers said their Singapore counterparts quoted baht selling offers in big $100 million lots against $10-30 million deals in normal market conditions.

"Sentiment was weak this morning and the market just reacted to a combination of negative factors. Economic indicators showed no signs of improvement, the stock market tumbled and the market speculated on whether there would be any economic policy changes," a dealer at a foreign bank said.
The Thai stock market index tumbled by the Wednesday lunch break to its lowest level since mid-June 1989.

Stock and money markets have been concerned in the past few days by suggestions by some members in Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's government that a change in the finance portfolio could help shore up market confidence.
Amnuay, who is attending a meeting of the Asian Development Bank in Japan, has not indicated that he would step down.
The Thai economy is in its worst shape in a decade with the gross domestic product projected to expand at about five to six percent this year against 6.7 in 1996 and 8.6 in 1995.
